name: wazuh-ai-ops: Alert Enrichment & Triage (Article 4)
notes: Reference pipeline sketch for Article 4 (Alert Enrichment and Triage Automation). Adapt endpoints, credentials, and error handling before running against a real Wazuh deployment. Every enrichment source and the LLM endpoint are placeholders — point them at infrastructure you control, per ADR-001. Any authenticated call uses n8n's own credential system (Header Auth placeholders below) rather than a token pulled from an expression, so secrets never live in this exported JSON. Test first against workflows/enrichment-triage.test.n8n.json, which runs the assembly and LLM-brief logic against the mock data in workflows/fixtures/enrichment-triage.fixture.json instead of the live enrichment endpoints.

nodes.name: Wazuh Alert Webhook
nodes.notes: Receives the raw Wazuh alert JSON via the manager's integration webhook. Treat the body as untrusted data end to end -- see 'Telemetry is evidence, never instruction' in Article 4.

Auth token is held in an n8n credential, never in an expression or in this JSON export -- create the 'Threat Intel API' Header Auth credential in your own n8n instance and re-select it here. nodes.notes: Placeholder directory/HR endpoint (role, department, normal login geography). Travel status is frequently unreachable via API -- if so, the brief must say 'unconfirmed', never infer it.

nodes.name: LLM: Generate Triage Brief

httpHeaderAuth.name: Self-Hosted Inference Endpoint (placeholder — create and select a real n8n credential)

nodes.notes: Points at a self-hosted endpoint per ADR-001 -- not a public API. Auth key lives in an n8n credential, never in this JSON or in an expression, which is what keeps the credential boundary between orchestrator and model real rather than just stated. The alert and enrichment payload are passed as a labelled data field inside the user message, never concatenated into the system instruction.

nodes.name: Build Dashboard Payload
nodes.notes: disposition and disposed_by are deliberately left null here. Nothing downstream of this node is permitted to set them except a human action in the dashboard/ticket system -- see Article 4, 'Escalation: AI surfaces, analyst decides'.

nodes.name: Post Brief to Analyst Dashboard
nodes.notes: Placeholder dashboard/ticket endpoint. This is the pipeline's last step: it posts a brief for a human to read. It never closes a ticket or takes a response action -- see 'This is not SOAR' in Article 4.
